title: Rerank variant arbitration and regional canary playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal:
Implement a repeatable, low-risk process for selecting and upgrading cross-encoder rerank variants across regions and locales while preserving latency SLOs and preventing quality regressions. The outcome is a documented arbitration matrix, automated smoke/regression checks, and a staged canary runbook that can be executed by SRE/ML infra teams.

Background:
We have multiple candidate cross-encoder models (dense, compact, quantized variants) that offer trade-offs between latency and pairwise quality. Customers in EMEA/APAC show different latency thresholds and locale distributions. Past upgrades have exposed latent regressions in long-tail locales and caused cost spikes when batches scaled. We need a formalized approach to: (1) pick candidate fallback and primary variants per region; (2) run automated multilingual regression suites; (3) staged canary and rollback triggers tied to quality and cost signals.

Success criteria / Acceptance:
- A documented arbitration matrix mapping workload profiles (qps, avg seq len, predominant locales) to preferred model variant and fallback.
- Automated regression harness that runs nightly and reports precision@k, MRR, latency P95, and cost-per-1000-tokens for baseline vs candidate.
- Canary orchestration template (console + infra runbook) that can roll forward or rollback based on configured thresholds within 24h.
- No detectable drop in production-quality metrics for top-10 locales (defined by traffic) during the staged rollout and no unplanned increase in 99th percentile latency >15%.
- Post-rollout postmortem and a telemetry dashboard link in the playbook.

Approach:
1) Build a model selection matrix: collect historical traffic slices (per-region qps, locale distribution, seq_len) and simulate cost/latency using offline profiler. Create heuristics to recommend primary and fallback variants per slice.
2) Regression harness: extend existing rerank harness to include stratified locale tests (long-tail sampling), adversarial prompts, and synthetic infra throttling to catch latency regressions. Harness should output JSON diffs and be schedulable in CI.
3) Canary orchestration: define small-percentage regional rollout (0.5% -> 5% -> 20%) with automated checks at each step. Checks include statistical tests on pairwise win-rate, latency P95, token cost delta, and error rates.
4) Rollback policy: automated immediate rollback for severe regressions (win-rate delta < -5% in top locales or latency P95 increase > 30%) and a human-in-the-loop review for marginal failures.
5) Observability: add model-level metrics to Console (per-route quality, cost delta, latency distribution) and a single-pane canary dashboard for quick triage.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative rollout reduces blast radius but increases time-to-value for cost/quality wins.
- Heavy synthetic tests increase signal but may produce false positives for rare production patterns; hence we combine synthetic with sampled production comparisons.
- Tight latency SLOs may force choosing compact variants that slightly degrade quality; arbitration matrix will encode acceptable quality-cost thresholds per customer tier.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1 (2025-06-02 to 2025-06-08): Data collection and profiler runs for target locales; draft arbitration matrix.
- Week 2 (2025-06-09 to 2025-06-15): Implement regression harness extensions and integrate long-tail sampling.
- Week 3 (2025-06-16 to 2025-06-22): Canary orchestration templates + Console dashboard hooks.
- Week 4 (2025-06-23 to 2025-06-30): Internal canary runs on staging; iterate thresholds; finalize runbook and run a dry-run with SRE.

Testing plan:
- Nightly regression jobs comparing baseline (prod) vs candidate across stratified slices.
- A/B test on 0.5% traffic with live shadow requests to verify KV/cache behavior.
- Spike tests to validate autoscaling/fallbacks.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Long-tail locale regressions not captured by tests. Mitigation: Include weighted sampling and a manual review step for locales with low volume before full rollout.
- Risk: Canary causing cache cold-start storms. Mitigation: Pre-warm KV caches and use staggered user cohorts.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps preventing quick rollback. Mitigation: Ensure canary dashboard ingests per-token latency and pairwise scoring metrics before enabling traffic.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Draft arbitration matrix (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/rerank/arbitration-matrix-149321
- Regression harness proto (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-harness/pull/842
- Canary runbook (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/rerank-canary-playbook-149321.pdf
- Console dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rerank-canary-149321

Rollout plan:
- Dry-run on staging with sampled production traffic window (48h).
- Stepwise regional canary: EU -> NA -> APAC with manual gating for APAC due to bandwidth/infrastructure differences.

Open decisions:
- Thresholds for win-rate and acceptable cost delta for P0 customers. Proposal: require win-rate >= -1% and cost delta <= 10% for roll-forward.
- Whether compact quantized variant should be default fallback in low-latency regions. Proposal: Use arbitration matrix to select per-region defaults and keep compact quantized as fallback for strict latency SLOs.

Acceptance / Done checklist:
- [ ] Arbitration matrix authored and approved by PM + ML lead.
- [ ] Regression harness runs nightly and artifacts stored.
- [ ] Canary runbook tested in staging and SRE run validated.
- [ ] Console canary dashboard visible to SRE/PM/ML.
- [ ] Post-rollout postmortem template created.
